content.content:
== Four Months for a Boat (completed)
- Never-Sold, who keeps the Chainbreakers' house in Blackrose, asked me to end an eleven-year Owing on the Tulm-Varo estate. She gave me a leaf of her own writing to put in the count-box in place of the real one, and the Owing's first price, 100 gold. I'm to speak to Rows-For-Another on the channel bank north of the town.
- Rows-For-Another told me the three things that hold her. Her leaf is in the keeper's count-box inside the estate house on the farm, and the keeper, Hulm-Tei, carries its key. His word could close the Owing. Brings-Them-Back, the estate's fetcher, watches the channel north of the bank. I'm to end her Owing by any of the three.
- I killed Brings-Them-Back on the channel. Nobody living knows the way to Rows-For-Another's home tree now. I'm to tell her the channel is clear, unless I end it another way first.
- I told Rows-For-Another the channel is clear. She will go by it once I have gone, and she gave me a word for Never-Sold. I'm to tell Never-Sold she is going.
- Cut loose. I told Never-Sold that Rows-For-Another has gone by the channel. Brings-Them-Back is dead, so nobody can follow her home. Never-Sold paid me in full and named me one of the Chainbreakers, and did not thank me for how.
== One Out of the Smoke (completed)
- Never-Sold sent me to the heirs' post on Blackrose's east shore. Three people the Rose holds are kept there, and one can be got out. She wants the one held for words, and gave me 100 gold. I'm to speak to the keeper of the post.
- I killed Third-Born Tsaxi at the heirs' post. Nobody is left to swear to any count, so any of the three can go, or all of them. I'm to tell them.
- I told Mends-Nets to go when I had gone. The other two stay. I'm to tell Never-Sold.
- I told Never-Sold that Mends-Nets came out, and that Walks-Far and Seven-Floods stayed. She said we will be called the people who loose killers, and that it will be true. She paid me 150 gold.

content.content:
== Four Months for a Boat (completed)
- Never-Sold, who keeps the Chainbreakers' house in Blackrose, asked me to end an eleven-year Owing on the Tulm-Varo estate. She gave me a leaf of her own writing to put in the count-box in place of the real one, and the Owing's first price, 100 gold. I'm to speak to Rows-For-Another on the channel bank north of the town.
- Rows-For-Another told me the three things that hold her. Her leaf is in the keeper's count-box inside the estate house on the farm, and the keeper, Hulm-Tei, carries its key. His word could close the Owing. Brings-Them-Back, the estate's fetcher, watches the channel north of the bank. I'm to end her Owing by any of the three.
- I killed Brings-Them-Back on the channel. Nobody living knows the way to Rows-For-Another's home tree now. I'm to tell her the channel is clear, unless I end it another way first.
- I told Rows-For-Another the channel is clear. She will go by it once I have gone, and she gave me a word for Never-Sold. I'm to tell Never-Sold she is going.
- Cut loose. I told Never-Sold that Rows-For-Another has gone by the channel. Brings-Them-Back is dead, so nobody can follow her home. Never-Sold paid me in full and named me one of the Chainbreakers, and did not thank me for how.
== One Out of the Smoke (completed)
- Never-Sold sent me to the heirs' post on Blackrose's east shore. Three people the Rose holds are kept there, and one can be got out. She wants the one held for words, and gave me 100 gold. I'm to speak to the keeper of the post.
- I killed Third-Born Tsaxi at the heirs' post. Nobody is left to swear to any count, so any of the three can go, or all of them. I'm to tell them.
- I told Mends-Nets to go when I had gone. The other two stay. I'm to tell Never-Sold.
- I told Never-Sold that Mends-Nets came out, and that Walks-Far and Seven-Floods stayed. She said we will be called the people who loose killers, and that it will be true. She paid me 150 gold.
== The Broker's Mercy (completed)
- Never-Sold sent me to Soulrest's dock, east of Lilmoth, where the Broker, Ussa-Rekh, holds a freed crew's tokens for one season more. She wants the tokens in the crew's hands, and she asked for a bound book with her name on it from his shelf. I'm to speak to Heavy-Rope at the head of the dock.
- Heavy-Rope told me the tokens are in the Broker's chest in his house, the north house of Soulrest. The key is on the Broker's belt and Feldril Nethri keeps his door. The berth-master Ra'Jhan pays for the season when it is sailed. I'm to free the crew by the chest, the Broker or the berth-master.
- I paid Feldril Nethri 30 gold. He unbarred the Broker's door for me. I'm to free the crew by the chest, the Broker or the berth-master.
- I took the crew's tokens from Ussa-Rekh's chest. His room was a poor man's room. I'm to bring the tokens to Heavy-Rope.
- The crew are free of the last season. Heavy-Rope gave me 150 gold of the crew's thanks. I'm to tell Never-Sold how it ended.
- Broken off. I told Never-Sold the crew have their tokens and the season is broken off. She gave me picks and named me a full Chainbreaker. The eleven at Thorn have lost their price.

content.text:
I finished the third Chainbreakers job, "The Broker's Mercy", and my journal now has no active objectives.

Here is how it went:
- **Getting in:** My Speech of 15 was too low to talk Heavy-Rope or Ra'Jhan round. I also couldn't afford the 1,000 gold for the season's hire. I paid Feldril Nethri 30 gold instead, and he unbarred the Broker's door.
- **The theft:** The house was empty, so I took Never-Sold's book and picked the chest unseen. That was stealing.
- **The ending:** I gave the crew's tokens to Heavy-Rope, who paid me 150 gold. Never-Sold took the book, gave me ten lockpicks, and named me a full Chainbreaker. The journal calls the outcome "Broken off".
- **The cost:** Ussa-Rekh said this season's hire was the price of eleven people at Thorn, where it is worst. I took the tokens anyway, so the eleven have lost that price. The journal says so, and I don't know what becomes of them.

The take is submitted. In it I said:
- **Liked:** the moral texture, and that the journal tracked the quests clearly.
- **Disliked:** many lines still show as unwritten "gist" placeholders.
- **Wanted to know:** what happens to the eleven at Thorn, and what the Broker was to Never-Sold.
